bills.title: ADMT/Employment Workplace AI Transparency
bills.summary: Would establish transparency requirements for the use of 'workplace AI tools' (ADMTs) that impact employment decisions or enable worker surveillance, requiring employers to provide advance notice and detailed disclosures to workers about how AI is used, what data is collected, and how it may affect roles, performance, or employment conditions, and maintain an updated inventory of such tools. Allows private rights of action with penalties, damages, and injunctive relief.
bills.status_detail: ADMT/Employment Bill Passes Committee

bills.title: California AI Transparency Act Enforcement Enhancement
bills.summary: Introduced by Asm. Wicks (D), this bill would increase the civil penalty for violations of the California AI Transparency Act to $5,500 per violation and reinforces enforcement mechanisms for ensuring public access to AI detection tools.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Asm. Wicks (D)

bills.title: Employer Technology Replacement Surcharge and Worker Retraining
bills.summary: Introduced by the Committee on Finance, Revenue, and Bonding, this bill would establish a framework for a surcharge on employers who replace workers with technology and use the proceeds to fund retraining and transition programs.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by the Committee on Finance, Revenue, and Bonding
sponsors: Committee on Finance, Revenue, and Bonding

bills.title: Idaho Conversational AI Services Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would require operators of 'conversational AI services' to disclose to minors that they are interacting with AI, develop protocols to respond to suicidal ideation from users, restrict engagement features designed to increase use (e.g., offering rewards at unpredictable intervals), and prohibit sexually explicit or manipulative content for minors. Also bars systems from fostering emotional or romantic dependence with minors and requires operators to provide parental controls and privacy tools for minor users. No private right of action.
bills.status_detail: Chatbot Bill Passes First Chamber

bills.title: Maryland Companion Chatbot Safety and Data Protection
bills.summary: Would regulate companion chatbots, combining safety, transparency, and data protection requirements. Requires self-harm detection and intervention protocols, persistent and recurring disclosures that users are interacting with AI, limits on collecting and using sensitive data including prohibiting use of emotional or mental health data to drive engagement, and establishment of a user complaint system. Notably treats chatbots as products subject to strict liability, imposing affirmative duty to prevent user harm, and allows individuals to bring claims for design, manufacturing, or marketing defects.
bills.status_detail: Chatbot Bill Passes First Chamber

bills.title: Maryland AI Behavioral Health Provider Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit AI systems from presenting themselves as behavioral health providers or being designed to deliver behavioral health care. Requires disclosures that users are interacting with AI and mandates protocols to detect and respond to self-harm or suicidal ideation. Includes exceptions for general wellness or guidance tools that do not claim to provide behavioral health care, and for AI used by licensed providers for administrative support.
bills.status_detail: Health / Chatbot Bill Passes First Chamber

bills.title: Maryland Food Retailer Surveillance Pricing Prohibition (Senate)
bills.summary: Companion bill to HB 895. Would prohibit food retailers and third-party delivery services from using protected class data to offer or price goods in a way that denies consumers equal access to benefits or services. Includes exceptions for standard practices such as promotions, loyalty programs, and pricing differences based on costs, supply, or demand.
bills.status_detail: Data Driven Pricing Bills Pass First Chamber

bills.title: Maryland Food Retailer Surveillance Pricing Prohibition (House)
bills.summary: Companion bill to SB 0387. Would prohibit food retailers and third-party delivery services from using protected class data to offer or price goods in a way that denies consumers equal access to benefits or services. Includes exceptions for standard practices such as promotions, loyalty programs, and pricing differences based on costs, supply, or demand.
bills.status_detail: Data Driven Pricing Bills Pass First Chamber

bills.title: Minnesota AI Mental Health Provider Prohibition with Chatbot and Ambient Listening Provisions
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill with additional chatbot-specific provisions. Would prohibit unlicensed AI-provided therapy and allow only limited administrative or support uses of AI under human oversight, with licensed professionals retaining full responsibility. Also introduces provisions around chatbots and 'ambient listening': requires chatbots in administrative support roles to disclose they are not human and direct users to seek help when mental health or self-harm issues arise, and imposes consent and transparency requirements for 'ambient listening' devices including disclosures on data use, storage, access, training, and the right to opt out without penalty.
bills.status_detail: Health / Chatbot Bill Passes Committee

bills.title: Minnesota AI Safety Frontier Models (RAISE Act-style)
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Jones (D), this bill is modeled on the New York RAISE Act but takes a broader approach, applying to any person that has trained an AI model (rather than distinguishing frontier developers) and lowering the threshold for critical risk incidents, while still establishing safety, transparency, and disclosure requirements.
bills.status_detail: AI Safety/Frontier Models bill introduced by Rep. Jones (D)

bills.title: New Jersey Grocery Surveillance Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit the use of personalized or surveillance-based algorithmic pricing for groceries and food items, making it an unlawful trade practice to vary prices based on personal data. Allows limited exceptions for cost-based pricing and broadly available discounts or loyalty programs, while restricting the use of personal data to those specific purposes. Also bans the use of electronic shelf labels connected to systems that enable personalized pricing.
bills.status_detail: Data-Driven Pricing Bill Passes Committee

bills.title: South Carolina Chatbot Minor Age Verification and Safeguards
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. Kimbrell (R), this bill would establish strict requirements for chatbot operators to verify user age, restrict minors' access to certain features without parental consent, and implement safeguards against harm.
bills.status_detail: Chatbots - introduced by Sen. Kimbrell (R)

bills.title: Vermont AI Advisory Council Study Bill
bills.summary: Amended to become a study bill establishing an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council to advise the state on AI use across government, including health care, education, and public services. The Council will conduct research, engage in public outreach, and develop recommendations on responsible AI use, including potential statutory changes and emerging issues like neurotechnology. Previously would have mandated disclaimers for AI-generated patient communications, restricted advertising and data collection for mental health chatbots, and enumerated a list of 'neurological rights'.
bills.status_detail: Health Bill Amended as a Study Bill and Passes Chamber

bills.title: Vermont AI Mental Health Restriction and Professional Responsibility
bills.summary: Similar to Illinois HB 1806, this bill would restrict AI use within mental health services to administrative and support functions, while requiring licensed professionals to retain full responsibility for care. Would prohibit AI from independently making diagnoses, treatment decisions, or generating treatment plans, and allow disciplinary action for violations. Would also classify the misuse of AI by mental health professionals as unprofessional conduct.
bills.status_detail: Health Bill Passes Chamber

bills.title: Washington GenAI Transparency and Provenance Law
bills.summary: Requires covered providers (those with over 1 million monthly users) to include provenance data (e.g., metadata or watermarking) in content that is generated or materially altered by their generative AI systems, with exclusions for video games and systems used solely for upscaling, noise reduction, or compression. Also requires government agencies to clearly and conspicuously disclose when consumers are interacting with an AI system; disclosures may be made via hyperlink. Takes effect February 1, 2027.
bills.status_detail: GenAI / Transparency Bill Signed into law

bills.title: Washington AI Companion Chatbot Safeguards Law (First Chatbot Law of 2026)
bills.summary: The first chatbot law enacted in 2026, requires operators of AI companion chatbots to implement safeguards for users. While framed around 'companion chatbots,' its reach may extend to other AI systems. Notable provisions: hourly disclosures for minors; new limits on engagement design targeting features that encourage emotional dependence, simulate relationships, discourage breaks, or promote isolation; required self-harm protocols including detection, crisis referrals, and public reporting of crisis referral notifications; and a private right of action without statutory damages. Takes effect January 1, 2027.
bills.status_detail: First Chatbot Law of the Year Signed

bills.title: GUARDRAILS Act - Repeal AI Executive Order
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Beyer (D-VA), the 'GUARDRAILS Act' would repeal President Trump's executive order 'Ensuring A National Policy Framework for AI' issued in December 2025. The bill would state that the executive order 'shall have no force or effect' and that no federal funds may be used to carry it out. Has 33 Democratic co-sponsors and a companion bill is set to be introduced in the Senate.
bills.status_detail: Democrats Introduce Bill to Repeal AI Executive Order

bills.title: Federal Chatbot Professional Impersonation Prohibition
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Mullin (D-CA), this bill would prohibit AI chatbot providers from falsely representing or implying that their systems are licensed medical, legal, or financial professionals, or that outputs are verified by such professionals. Extends existing professional impersonation protections to AI systems. Would also direct the FTC to issue guidance establishing clear compliance standards for industry.
bills.status_detail: Chatbot Bill Introduced by Rep. Mullin (D-CA)

bills.title: Federal AI Digital Impersonation Fraud Criminalization
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. Sheehy (R-MT) and Sen. Rochester (D-DE), this bill would criminalize AI-driven digital impersonation fraud and establish regulatory and technical frameworks for detection and prevention. House companion bill: HR 7786.
bills.status_detail: Liability Bill Introduced

bills.title: Federal AI Digital Impersonation Fraud Criminalization (House)
bills.summary: House companion to S 3982. Would criminalize AI-driven digital impersonation fraud and establish regulatory and technical frameworks for detection and prevention.
bills.status_detail: Liability Bill Introduced (House companion to S 3982)

bills.title: Arizona App Store Accountability Act - Age Verification and Parental Consent
bills.summary: Passed out of committee with an amendment on March 25 (previously passed the House on March 5). While the bill initially would have regulated minors' use and access of social media and harmful content, the bill now follows an App Store Accountability Act-style framework. App store providers must conduct age verification and obtain parental consent and share information related to age range and parent consent with developers via age signals.
bills.status_detail: ASAA Bill PASSED COMMITTEE with amendment on March 25; previously passed House on March 5

bills.title: Georgia Consumer Privacy Protection Act (Gutted)
bills.summary: The proposed Georgia Consumer Privacy Protection Act, which passed the Senate last year but was held in the House committee, appears to be dead. The committee favorably reported a substitute that guts and amends the bill, replacing it with a tax credit bill.
bills.status_detail: Comprehensive Privacy Bill Gutted and Amended - committee substitute replaces it with a tax credit bill

bills.title: Maine Maryland-Style Comprehensive Privacy with Data Minimization
bills.summary: Maine's comprehensive privacy bill, heavily inspired by Maryland's law, has re-passed the House after being amended during the concurrence process. The bill will be engrossed and return to the Senate for their concurrence vote. One remaining difference: the Senate version includes an exemption for political organizations.
bills.status_detail: Comprehensive Privacy RE-PASSED HOUSE after amendment during concurrence process

bills.title: Maryland Privacy Amendment - Immigration Enforcement Data Sales Prohibition
bills.summary: As amended, would prohibit a controller from knowingly selling personal data to a governmental unit that, within the prior 6 months, has engaged in or supported civil immigration enforcement through the provision of personnel or material resources. Other changes: expanding the definition of precise geolocation data to extend to information identifying the location of a mobile device or vehicle (within 1,750 feet), adding a sensitive data catch-all for inferences used to indicate a category of sensitive data, and narrowing the legal compliance exception with respect to civil immigration enforcement.
bills.status_detail: Privacy Amendment on Immigration Enforcement PASSED HOUSE

bills.title: Michigan Kids Code
bills.summary: Passed out of committee on March 25. Now on third reading but no immediate vote expected since the Senate has adjourned until April 14.
bills.status_detail: Michigan Kids Code Passed Committee on March 25; now on third reading

bills.title: Minnesota Autonomous Vehicle Bill with Privacy Provisions
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Sencer-Mura (D) on March 23. While most of the bill is outside the scope of privacy updates, it provides that an 'on-demand autonomous vehicle network' would be subject to the Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act.
bills.status_detail: Autonomous Vehicle Bill Introduced on March 23

bills.title: New Jersey Children's Data Protection Bill
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. Vitale (D) on March 19. This minor-focused social media privacy bill would require covered entities reasonably likely to be accessed by children to conduct data protection impact assessments (DPIAs), implement default privacy settings for minors, and restrict certain processing activities involving minor data.
bills.status_detail: Children's Data Protection Bill Introduced on March 19

bills.title: Oklahoma Comprehensive Privacy Law (Virginia-style)
bills.summary: Oklahoma becomes the 20th state with a comprehensive privacy law. Governor Stitt signed SB 546 on March 20. This is a standard, Virginia-style law that will go into effect on January 1, 2027.
bills.status_detail: Comprehensive Privacy Law ENACTED - signed by Governor Stitt on March 20, 2026

bills.title: South Dakota Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Privacy Act
bills.summary: South Dakota enacted a direct-to-consumer genetic testing privacy law after Governor Rhoden signed SB 49 on March 23. This law regulates direct-to-consumer genetic testing, including consumer data rights, consent requirements, and data security obligations.
bills.status_detail: Genetic Privacy Law ENACTED - signed by Governor Rhoden on March 23, 2026

bills.title: Utah UCPA Amendment on Vehicle Privacy
bills.summary: Governor Cox signed HB 357 on March 19. This bill amends the Utah Consumer Privacy Act, expanding coverage to motor vehicle manufacturers who collect personal data through a vehicle data collection system and imposing requirements for in-vehicle privacy controls.
bills.status_detail: UCPA Amendment on Vehicle Privacy ENACTED - signed by Governor Cox on March 19, 2026

bills.title: Vermont Data Broker Registration Update
bills.summary: The House passed H.211 on March 25. Would update Vermont's data broker registration law. Changes include updating the definition of brokered personal information (to align more with definitions in state comprehensive privacy laws), requiring data brokers to provide consumers with a mechanism to have their brokered personal information deleted, and directing the Vermont Secretary of State to study the feasibility of creating a Delete Act-style accessible deletion mechanism.
bills.status_detail: Data Broker Update PASSED HOUSE on March 25
